text:
elaine (product): Heads-up — ACME asked if we can let customers temporarily shrink their reserved pool for short maintenance windows. They want up to 20% reduction for 2h windows, 4x/week, for the next 6 months, in exchange for a 5% price credit. Can we productize a 'withdrawal window' feature?

mike (eng-platform): Quick clarifying Q — when they shrink, does that capacity get returned to the global free pool for others to consume, or is it held as "staged" and only reassignable after X?

elaine (product): They expect the capacity to be re-used (so other tenants can use it) but we must guarantee they can reclaim it at the end of each window.

lee (eng-sre): Warning — reclaimability + re-use = preemption complexity. We'll need deterministic eviction order and a strong fallback so we don't blow SLAs. Also fragmentation risk if many tenants do this.

sara (sales): This is a recurring ask from regulated customers. If we can offer it as a contract add-on, it unlocks a few enterprise deals. Need clear price+SLA language.

omar (finance): Put an estimate on revenue delta. 5% credit vs churn risk. We should model: expected enrolled customers * avg commit * credit * adoption rate (start conservative).

natalie (cs): Support y/n — this will increase onboarding steps. We need observability per tenant (how many windows used, failures to reclaim, reclaim latency). Also a playbook for customer-impact incidents.

mike (eng-platform): Implementation idea: introduce a lightweight schedule object on the commitment that specifies windows; runtime exposes `withdrawal_windows` and `reclaim_window_seconds`. Example config:
```yaml
commit: 1000vram_units
withdrawal_windows:
  - dow: [Mon,Wed,Fri]
    start: "01:00"
    duration_minutes: 120
    reduction_pct: 20
    reclaim_timeout_secs: 300
```
We'd need: scheduler changes, scoring tweaks to allow opportunistic fill, and a reclaim handshake.

lee (eng-sre): +1 to schema. Also need a safety circuit: max concurrent withdrawals globally and per-region so oncall doesn't get flooded. If reclaim fails repeatedly, auto-escalate and suspend withdrawals for that customer.

elaine (product): For launch criteria let's list minimal set: 1) reclaim success >= 99% in canary, 2) reclaim latency < 30s p95, 3) billing credit calculation validated, 4) docs + contracts ready, 5) support playbook exists. Anything missing?

mike (eng-platform): Also add infra metric: extra tail latency impact on co-tenants < 5% relative. And a rollout plan: internal pilot -> few trusted customers -> broad GA. Dev estimate: ~3 sprints for core runtime + 1 sprint for billing/console + 1 for docs/support.

omar (finance): We'll need a billing signal: time-windowed credit calculation. Do we credit per-window or monthly aggregate? I'd prefer per-window (simpler to reconcile), but want a reconciliation view for contracts.

sara (sales): Contracts team wants template text: max reductions, guaranteed reclaim SLA, escalation path, and a test window clause (we need an acceptance demo before sign). I can draft language once product agrees.

natalie (cs): Support test plan: simulate reclaim failures, simulate mid-window priority shifts, and validate alerts. Also add a customer-facing dashboard: scheduled windows, last reclaim status, credit history.

mike (eng-platform): Dev note: we should expose a dry-run mode and a simulation endpoint so CS/Sales can demo without touching live capacity. Implementation might reuse existing preemption machinery but needs a softer preempt type to avoid data loss.

deploy-bot: RFC created: https://rfc.internal/withdrawal-windows (draft). Please add comments.

elaine (product): Next steps: Mike to own RFC + runtime spec, Lee to own SRE runbook and circuit breakers, Natalie to own support playbook + acceptance tests, Sara to draft contract language, Omar to produce revenue model. Can we get an ETA for RFC + rough dev estimate in next week?

mike (eng-platform): I'll post RFC comments by EOD Friday and attach a rough milestone: prototyping sprint (1), core runtime (3), billing & UI (1), pilot & monitoring (1).

lee (eng-sre): I'll sketch runbook and a global limiter proposal tomorrow. Also want an oncall incident metric set: reclaim_failures, reclaim_latency_p95, concurrent_withdrawals.

natalie (cs): I'll build the demo script and required dashboards.

sara (sales): I'll sync with legal & send a draft contract template by next Tue.

omar (finance): I'll model two scenarios and post the numbers into the RFC as a table.

elaine (product): Great — thanks all. Putting this on next roadmap sync as "withdrawal windows pilot". If anyone wants to be an early reviewer ping me. :thumbsup:
